newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Alan Fels indicated Westpac's A$1.4 billion takeover bid for the Bank of Melbourne was unlikely to overcome Federal Government regulation hurdles despite the Wallis inquiry into the financial system calling for a change in such regulations. Professor Fels said there was still a very real need for regional banks to maintain competition in the industry. Page 1.

A survey by labour hire firm Recruitment Solutions has found 32 percent of businesses in metropolitan Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane were the subject of an unfair dismissal claim in the last 12 months. This suggests the dismissal laws may have been absurd, but also that businesses lacked skills in recruitment, counselling and personnel practices. Page 3.

The Metal Trades Federation of Unions has endorsed a campaign of 24-hour stoppages if employers use new Federal legislation to pare back award conditions. Members will vote for strike action unless demands to maintain the award's existing conditions and scope are met by employers. Page 3.

The Federal Government has been urged not to make major changes to business taxation without consultation or before a report of a review of business programs is received. Senior Australian businessmen, including Business Council of Australia president Stn Wallis, have sent a letter to Prime Minister John Howard raising a number of concerns. Page 3.

A recent equity issue from Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd, where 65 per cent of the total stock is held by just three stockholders, has prompted investors to consider a rival index to the Australian Stock Exchange's All Ordinaries Index. There is dispute about the current weighting system where a company is not capitalised at the value of its liquidity. Page 35.

Sigma Pharmaceuticals, a leading pharmacy wholesaling group, has reported a net profit of over $A4 million despite intense competition for a greater national market share. The low net profit is blamed on low sales margins experienced industry-wide. Page 5.

BP Australia, a subsidiary of British Petroleum Plc, is reviewing its operations in Australia and applying pressure on the Government to fast-track plans to deregulate the petroleum industry. Job losses at BP are not envisaged, but the company must further trim costs in the likelihood of an increased downturn this year. Page 40.
THE AUSTRALIAN

On the first day after the tabling of the Wallis report into banking services, AMP Society and GIO Ltd both declared their ambitions to grow by acquisition. Competition regulator Professor Allan Fels yesterday stated he is likely to approve a takeover of one of the biggest four banks by an insurance group. Page 21.

Foster's Brewing Group has announced an $A18 million investment to build a brewery in Mumbai. This would make Foster's the first foreign brewer to have permission to produce beer in the heavily protected Indian market. Foster's has previously invested $130 million in three Chinese breweries. Page 21.

The Commonwealth Bank has launched a securitisation program for its vehicle lease portfolio. CBA is the nation's biggest funder of vehicle fleet leases in the last year, and has funded the State Government fleets in South Australia and New South Wales for a combined total of $A350 million. Page 21.

Lend Lease Ltd has reached an agreement to buy the A$35 billion Equitable Real Estate Investment Management group from The Equitable Companies Inc, part of the AXA insurance and financial services group. This will give Lend Lease A$44 billion in real estate assets when combined with assets from the Yarmouth asset and property management group, acquired in 1993. Page 21.

The West Australian Government confirmed yesterday it is introducing a levy on gold production from January 1, 1998, starting at 1.25 percent, and increasing to 2.5 percent. Miners have previously warned this would break the back of the industry which is suffering from depressed prices and rising production costs. Page 23.

BP Australia Ltd has announced a review of retail operations as the annual net profit of the petrol giant fell 38 percent to A$124 million. The main factors of the poor result are believed to be strong competition in the retail market and depressed refining margins. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In the wake of the Wallis report's argument for relaxing the ban on foreign takeovers, the ANZ Banking Group has emerged as a prime target for a takeover bid. ANZ was seriously approached by the giant Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp in the early 1990s but was rejected due to Labor's ban on foreign takeovers at the time. Page 25.

Final bids have been placed in the first round of airport privatisations. The sale of the Melbourne, Perth and Brisbane airports is expected to raise about $A3 billion, with a Commonwealth Bank -led group favourite to buy Brisbane Airport and a Macquarie Bank syndicate favourite for Melbourne Airport. Page 27.

Lend Lease Corp will become the world's largest property funds manager after an agreement to purchase the US-based Equitable Real Estate Investment Management for $A510 million. This purchase furthers Lend Lease's ambition of developing a global property funds operation, adding to existing developments in the United Kingdom, Asia and Australia. Page 25.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Allan Fels has repeated his concerns over the Wallis inquiry's recommendation that consumer protection should be handled by a new regulatory body. Professor Fels was satisfied with other rcommendations on consumer protection and is confident of a resolution. Page 25.

The Australian Consumers' Association has warned the Wallis report's recommendations regarding the use of personal customer information for multiple purposes by financial institutions could penalise large groups of people unaware of the situation. Financial groups have argued the process will become more cost-efficient as they increase their range of products and services. Page 29.

In the first time an international brewer has been permitted to buy into India, the Foster's Brewing Group has acquired a 51 percent stake in a brewery in Maharashtra state. Shareholders in Foster's have been warned it could take several years before profits will be yielded. Page 30.
THE AGE

The Wallis report on the financial sector recommendations that a single "mega-regulator" for banks be installed have come under fire from Australia's largest banks. Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray described the proposal as "absolutely wrong" while ANZ Bank and Westpac have argued the Reserve Bank remain the main banking sector regulator. Page B1.

Property management and development group Lend Lease has stepped up its international expansion plans with the announcement of plans to purchase major US property manager Equitable Real Estate Investment Management (ERE) for A$510 million. Page B1.

Australian Competition and Consumer chairman Professor Alan Fels is pressuring to retain a role in consumer protection in the financial sector, despite the Wallis inquiry's recommendation that such protection be moved into the arena of the new Corporation and Financial Services Commission. Professor Fels said he would be concerned for consumers if the ACCC lost its role in policing part five of the Trade Practices Act. Page B1.

A consortium including the City of Melbourne last night remained the favourite to buy the Melbourne Airport. The drawn-out auction took final bids yesterday as the consortium, led by Macquarie Bank and including National Mutual and Manchester Airport, is believed to have bid up to A$1.2 billion. Page B3.

Foster's Brewing Group has increased its Asian presence with the 51 per cent acquisition of a brewing venture in Maharashtra state, India. The A$18 million investment has been described as long-term by Foster's as the group warned shareholders it may take several years before profits were yielded. Page B2.

BP Australia, a division of British Petroleum plc, announced a review of its operations in Australia saying its returns in the retail market were "abysmal". The review announcement by BP is also believed to increase pressure on the Federal Government to continue with plans to deregulate the petroleum industry. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
